rows.name: multipart-pause-1500
rows.question: For exactly ten thousand elements and one hundred ninety two threads per block, compute the minimum number of blocks needed to cover every element. Also report the active threads in the final block and the number of launched threads that need a bounds check. Explain the arithmetic.
rows.recognizedQuestion: For example, ten thousand elements and one hundred ninety two threads per block compute the minimum number of blocks needed to cover every element Also report the active threads in the final block and the number of launched threads that need a bounce check Explain the arithmetic
rows.answer:
You need 53 blocks. Since 10,000 = 52 × 192 + 16, 52 blocks cover 9,984 elements, and one more block covers the remaining 16.

The final block has 16 active threads and 176 excess threads, because 53 × 192 = 10,176 threads are launched. Interpreting “bounce check” as “bounds check,” all 10,176 threads should evaluate `if (index < 10000)`, and the 176 excess threads fail that check and skip processing.

rows.name: switch-topic
rows.question: Switch topics. Why does snapshot isolation permit write skew even if both read-check-write sequences run in atomic transactions?
rows.recognizedQuestion: Switch topics. Why does snapshot isolation permit write skew even if both read-check-write sequences run in atomic transactions?
rows.answer:
Atomicity makes each transaction all-or-nothing; it does not make concurrent transactions behave as if they ran one at a time. Under snapshot isolation, both can read the same old snapshot, pass their checks, and commit updates to different rows without a write-write conflict.

For example, Alice and Bob are both on call, and at least one must remain. Each transaction sees the other person on call and marks its own person off call. Since they update different rows, both can commit, leaving nobody on call: that is write skew. Serializable isolation would prevent both from committing with that outcome.

review.note: Atomicity versus serializability correctly distinguished; old snapshots and disjoint-row writes allow both doctors off call; impossible serial result and serializable prevention correct.
review.usefulPrefix: Atomicity makes each transaction all-or-nothing; it does not make concurrent transactions behave as if they ran one at a time.
